The name Baraj is a reminder of this might and is often given as a name to instill a sense of strength and resilience in the bearer.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hawaiyal's Tarikh al-Buldan mentions Baraj as a city in the province of Aleppo, Syria, during the early Islamic period in the 8th century. It was a significant agricultural center and one of the main stops on the trade route from the Mediterranean to the Euphrates River.

Al-Idrisi's Geography of the World describes Baraj as a city in the province of Qinnasrin, Syria, during the late medieval period in the 12th century. It was an important market town and a center for the production of textiles, particularly silk.
